description:
One plugin instead of dozens. 554 tools, and they agree with each other.

Rooster One does the work that would otherwise take dozens of separate plugins, and it does it from one place, on one set of numbers.

Dozens of plugins means dozens of different vendors, dozens of renewal dates to keep track of, dozens of update cycles that have to keep working alongside each other, and a different support desk to write to depending on which part has gone wrong. One plugin means one licence, one update, one place to ask, and one thing for WordPress to load on every request instead of dozens.

What is actually in it: a full SEO engine that replaces Yoast or AIOSEO. Product recommendations built from your real sales. Role, wholesale and tiered pricing. Meta, Google Ads, GA4 and TikTok measurement, sent server-side so an ad blocker cannot silence it. Sixteen couriers with vouchers, labels, tracking and daily closings. Marketplace feeds and order import for Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, Etsy, Amazon and more. Side cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist, quote requests for catalogue shops, swatches, trust badges. Popups and scheduled announcements. Abandoned-cart recovery, email and web push campaigns, audiences. Surveys, competitions and events. Invoices, packing slips and credit notes. A GDPR consent banner with a cookie scanner. The EU withdrawal button that Directive 2023/2673 now requires. And an AI assistant that answers from your own catalogue rather than making things up.

That is 188 pages and the 554 tools inside them, and there is a written description of what every one of them is for.

Why one plugin rather than dozens

Because separate plugins cannot see what the others know, so they disagree, and each one works the same thing out again while your customer waits.

Rooster One measures your whole business on a schedule instead: every product, page, customer, order and session, written into flat tables. Which products sell and which never do, which pages are read, who bought and who nearly did. The SEO engine, the recommendations, the audiences, the ad ROI report and the AI assistant then all read those same tables. That is why they agree, and why the plugin gets faster to use as you switch more of it on: the heavy work already happened, before the request arrived. The trade-off is timing and we would rather say so plainly. A figure is only as new as its last run.

And it is one plugin to load, not dozens

This part has nothing to do with how well any plugin is written. WordPress loads every active plugin on every request, before it knows whether that request needs it: a file to read from disk, hooks to register, options to fetch, a translation catalogue to load. That toll is paid on the home page, on every admin screen and on every REST call, by every plugin, including the ones that will do nothing at all on that particular request. A site carrying a hundred of them pays it a hundred times before a single line of useful work happens.

Rooster One is one plugin, and the parts you have not switched on register nothing. On Pro, the storefront is served by a separate lightweight runtime rather than the admin half, so your customer’s page load carries the code that draws the page and not the code that runs the shop.

Everything is off by default. It installs beside your current SEO plugin, pixel manager and consent tool and changes nothing until you switch a piece on.

Rooster One runs on your own server. Everything it ever sends to an outside service, and what triggers it, is listed under “What does Rooster One send to an outside service, and when?” in the FAQ below.

The free version is a complete product, not a demo: 754 of the 1,268 screens, tools and actions are in it. Pro adds the operational half and the separate front-end runtime plugin.

Who builds it

Rooster One is built by Oxford Metadata Ltd, whose organisation is approved under Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program for dual-use security work such as penetration testing and vulnerability research. That is the same discipline the plugin’s own defensive features come out of: the bot filtering, the form captcha, the consent and proof-of-consent log, and the login hardening. The AI features run on Anthropic Claude for chat and reasoning and Voyage AI for embeddings.

It reads your site for what it is

  • Shop — sales and add-to-carts are the measure.
  • Catalogue — products published but not sold; engagement is the measure.
  • Content — no WooCommerce; visits, engagement and forms are the measure.

Auto-detected, overridable in one click. Scoring, cornerstones and applicable signals all follow from it.

You can find all of it

Ctrl+K reaches 742 places: 188 pages and the 554 tools inside them, each one openable directly. All Features lists every one, with pinnable favourites, and prints the figure for your own install. Every page carries a written description of what you can do there, and that text feeds the search.

What gets measured

Computed on a schedule, stored flat. Everything below reads these.

  • Product vitals — velocity, out-of-stock history, price history, basket role, returns, and a 0–100 demand score.
  • Content vitals — reach, engagement, freshness and a content-demand score for every post, page and custom type.
  • Customer vitals — an omnichannel profile: purchases, affinities, lifecycle stage, survey answers, return risk.
  • Session and attribution rollups — engagement joined to conversion on one session id, with landing page, campaign and five UTMs.
  • Effective prices — every price rule resolved ahead of time into one row per product per audience.

The features

AI chat & semantic search

  • Chat widget on Anthropic Claude, grounded in your catalogue — only real, in-stock items with exact links.
  • Semantic search on Voyage AI embeddings across products, posts, pages and terms.
  • A knowledge base you control, with identity guardrails so it cannot mis-describe you.
  • Chat analytics — what was asked, how it was rated, which questions found nothing, which chats ended in an order.
  • Related content on articles, guides, listings and products, from the same index. Added automatically to the content types you choose, or placed by hand with the AIEO Related content block or the [aieo_semantic_related] shortcode; either can be narrowed to one kind of content, so a listing recommends listings rather than products.

SEO engine

A drop-in replacement for AIOSEO, Yoast or Rank Math. Stays gated behind your current SEO plugin until you switch over; a read-only importer for all three and a head-parity check are included.

  • Head, canonical, robots, Open Graph, Twitter and JSON-LD, assembled once into a cache.
  • Commerce schema from the same tables — ProductGroup + hasVariant, per-variant colour, gtin, brand, shipping and return policy.
  • AI titles and descriptions written against the live SERP. Drafts await approval, or run on Autopilot.
  • Opportunity grid — traffic × conversion: hidden gem, intent mismatch, defend, prune.
  • Rank tracking (optional DataForSEO, under your spend cap).
  • Redirects and 404s, slug monitor, static sitemap, robots.txt, alt-text filling, EU Omnibus history, hreflang, Local SEO.

Selling more

  • Recommendations — up-sell, cross-sell and same-need alternatives from your real sales patterns.
  • Rails you order by drag-and-drop, block and classic themes, with custom slots.
  • Pricing engine — role and wholesale prices, brand discounts, loyalty tiers, points, free gifts. Stacked, resolved ahead of time.
  • Merchandising — swatches, labels, trust badges, payment logos, galleries, layout builder, custom tabs, one master button style.
  • Lift measurement — the incremental orders and revenue the engine adds.

Cart, checkout, recovery

  • Side cart, sticky add-to-cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist.
  • Quote requests for catalogue shops — an ask-for-a-price card on products you do not sell online, a quote basket the shopper grows as they browse, and the browsing trail behind each request. Booked as valued leads per campaign, so a catalogue stops scoring EUR 0.00.
  • Saved and abandoned carts — share and resume, cookieless restore that survives CDN caching.
  • Checkout tuning — distraction-free checkout with A/B assignment, minimum order, and business-invoice fields.
  • Full block and classic parity.

Reaching customers

  • Audiences — top, lapsed, lookalike, abandoned-cart, reactivation, competition entrants. Recomputed nightly.
  • Automated campaigns — abandoned cart, win-back, birthday, back in stock, post-purchase. Email and web push, quiet hours honoured.
  • Social posts from your catalogue, competitions on any Gravity Form, surveys scored into NPS and voice-of-customer.

Knowing what worked

  • Server-side measurement you own — Meta CAPI, GA4, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions, TikTok Events API. Deduplicated, sent after the order is saved, with a daily safety net.
  • Consent / GDPR CMP — first-party banner, Consent Mode v2, proof-of-consent log, cookie scanner.
  • ROI Wizard — orders, revenue, cost, net, ROAS and ROI by engine, offer, channel, campaign or creative.
  • Ad spend typed, by CSV, or nightly from Google Ads / Meta / TikTok. Conversion goals for non-shops.
  • Insights Chat — ask your shop questions in wp-admin. Customers pseudonymised, no data export.

Running the shop

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon → native WooCommerce orders. The catalogue importer runs it in reverse.
  • Streaming feeds — ready-made templates for Amazon Inventory Loader, BestPrice, eBay File Exchange, eFood, EMAG, Etsy, Facebook Product Catalog, Facebook Marketplace, Google Shopping, Google Local, Google AdWords Custom Remarketing, Shopflix, Skroutz, Tolstoy and Wolt, plus Generic CSV and a fully custom builder.
  • Sixteen couriers — vouchers, labels, COD, tracking, bulk printing, daily closings. ACS, BOX NOW, Courier Center, ELTA, Geniki Taxydromiki, Speedex, DHL Express, FedEx, UPS, USPS, Royal Mail, DHL Paket, Colissimo, BRT, Correos Express, Sendcloud — plus a manual carrier for one with no API.
  • Order documents — invoices, packing slips, proformas, credit notes. Singly or merged across a date range.
  • Delivery economics — real break-even free shipping from your carrier costs, per-carrier × zone P&L.
  • Operational intelligence — stock recovery, missing hot sellers, out-of-stock predictor, branch stock, barcode scanning, optional ERP.

The withdrawal button — Directive (EU) 2023/2673

Every EU distance seller must now give consumers a prominent, permanently available button to declare withdrawal electronically. No transition period.

  • A real button, for the whole statutory period.
  • 14 calendar days from receipt — computed from delivery, not the order date.
  • Guests included. An account is offered afterwards, never required.
  • No reason, no prior contact, partial withdrawal by item and quantity.
  • Acknowledgement on a durable medium with content, date and time.
  • Cancellation stays distinct from withdrawal — one you may refuse, the other you may not.
  • Return vouchers checked by an operator before the customer sees them. Ships disabled.

Content, blocks and regional selling

  • Events with RSVP and self-registration, FAQ accordions, Store Pages, Food & Beverages option groups, Google reviews, Media Cleanup that quarantines before it deletes.
  • Dozens of server-rendered blocks — store, product, recommendation, swatch, brand, category, blog, competition and event, plus Custom Slot regions.
  • Regional checkout — COD by country or courier, “from X,XX €” labels before a postcode is entered, and per-country payment and shipping rules.

Speed and resilience

  • Pre-computed into flat tables; the storefront reads single cached rows.
  • A thin front-end runtime plugin (Pro) serves the storefront even when the admin plugin is trimmed from the request.
  • Self-healing jobs re-arm after updates, stay dormant until used, and collapse runaway third-party tasks.
  • Tables are never dropped on update, activation or deactivation — only on explicit uninstall.

Free and Pro

GPLv3. The free version is a complete, working product — not a demo with the useful parts removed.

GPLv3 throughout. There are three separate things here, and it is worth being precise about which is which, because two of them are called “Pro”.

1. This plugin, free. A complete, working product, not a demo with the useful parts removed: AI chat and semantic search, the whole SEO engine, pricing and merchandising, storefront features, measurement and consent, product feeds and marketplace feed export, courier fulfilment across all sixteen carriers, the block library, Ctrl+K — and the complete withdrawal button. That last is a legal obligation for every EU distance seller; charging for it would be a poor thing to do.

2. A Pro subscription (or the 14-day trial), activated by connecting the site to your Rooster One account. No per-feature keys. It unlocks the Pro screens whose code is already inside this download:

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon.
  • Attribution and ROI — dashboard, ROI Wizard, ad-spend connectors, shipping cost against margin.
  • Audiences and campaigns — audience builder, email and web-push flows, social posts, AI-suggested offers.
  • Customer intelligence — customer lookup, surveys, cancellations and returns analysis, chat analytics.
  • Insights Chat, events and competitions, Action Scheduler cleanup.

3. Two companion plugins, included with a Pro subscription and installed separately. A subscription on its own does not put their code on your server, so these screens ask you to install the plugin rather than pretending to work:

  • Rooster One Runtime — serves the storefront, SEO head, sitemap and redirects without loading the admin half. The biggest single speed difference between free and Pro.
  • Rooster One Pro — carries six engines this download does not contain: supplier invoice scanning, the accounting and ERP connectors (Entersoft, Galaxy, Soft1, Zoho Books, and Oxygen supplier sync), the catalogue importer for building a product source from a supplier feed, the product exchanger for sharing content between WP sites, the duplicate-product merge engine that auto detects simple products and converts them to variations, and semantic internal linking.

Everything Pro-locked stays visible with an explanation of what it does, and where a screen also needs the Pro plugin it says so before you buy, not after.

Optional integrations

Rooster One runs entirely on your own server. Nothing below is required for the plugin to work — each is an opt-in add-on you enable only if you want that capability, using your own account.

  • Rooster AI credits (rooster.systems) — powers the AI chat, AI SEO copy and Insights Chat via Anthropic Claude and Voyage AI embeddings, with no per-provider API keys to manage.
  • Recommendations service (eshop-optimizer.com) — graph-database up-sell/cross-sell analysis of your order history.
  • DataForSEO — optional keyword rank tracking under a spend cap you set.
  • Ad and measurement platforms — Google Ads, GA4, Meta and TikTok, each independently selectable.
  • Couriers and marketplaces — your own carrier and marketplace accounts, for vouchers and order import.
  • Google Places / Search Console for location data and search performance.

upgrade_notice.11.1.1: Settings wording that could get stuck in English now follows your shop's language, and an update repairs values already saved; anything you typed yourself is untouched. upgrade_notice.11.1.0: Pro features now carry their engines in the Rooster One Pro plugin: if you use the catalogue importer, product feeds between sites or duplicate products, update Rooster One Pro to 11.1.0 as well or those screens will tell you it is missing. upgrade_notice.11.0.9: A repair release for 11.0.8. Two command-line features shipped broken in the packaged build even though they worked in development: onboarding a large catalogue with wp aieo semantic onboard, and the push notification controls in the hosting panel. upgrade_notice.11.0.8: Adds staff sign-in protection (TOTP two-factor, a private sign-in address, and lockout on repeated guessing - all shipped off) and, for shops on the semantic engine, a large reliability release: chunked onboarding that survives big catalogues, vocabulary approvals that take effect on their own, an optional auto-accept mode for link suggestions, and two identity-layer corrections. upgrade_notice.11.0.7: Recommended for every site showing the cookie banner, and for any shop whose mobile pages feel slow to respond. upgrade_notice.11.0.5: Recommended for every shop charging a cash-on-delivery surcharge. upgrade_notice.10.1: Recommended for every shop selling at a distance in the EU. Adds a complete withdrawal-button implementation for Directive (EU) 2023/2673, which applies with no transition period once your member state has transposed it: a permanent button that works for guests, no reason and no prior contact required, partial withdrawal on multi-item orders, and an acknowledgement email on a durable medium in your shop's own language. Ten international courier drivers added — DHL Express, FedEx, UPS, USPS, Royal Mail, DHL Paket, Sendcloud, Colissimo, BRT and Correos Express. The withdrawal feature ships disabled; switch it on once your returns policy and terms are ready. Also fixes a DHL Paket billing number that could be accepted against another account, and courier settings being blanked on save.
upgrade_notice.10.0: Recommended for everyone. Adds a searchable index of every screen in the plugin (Ctrl+K from anywhere), a written description on every page and tab, and a site-profile badge in the header showing whether Rooster One reads your site as a shop, a catalogue or a content site. All source strings are now English with the original wording preserved as translations, so nothing your customers see changes. Also fixes a bug where the AI settings form could still store OpenAI — a provider dropped in May — and corrects a misleading AI-credits message that sent operators to re-check a connector that was already working.
upgrade_notice.9.5: Recommended for everyone, and important if you run on multisite or host several shops on one server. Updating or deactivating no longer drops any database table — a network deactivation previously discarded twelve working tables plus your live sessions and session archive, and two schema migrations could empty the purchase-history rollup or your stored survey responses on update. Report windows such as "this month" now follow the timezone in Settings → General rather than the server clock, so figures no longer shift when your host is in a different timezone from your shop. Recommendation caches are cleared once on upgrade, so expect a brief cache-miss on product pages immediately afterwards.
upgrade_notice.9.2: Recommended if your site has ever been restored, migrated or cloned. Database backups omit stored routines by default, which could leave the surveys, web-push, product-needs and session-analytics jobs failing every night with "PROCEDURE … does not exist" — permanently, since reactivating the plugin did not rebuild them. upgrade_notice.9.1: Recommended for everyone. Fixes a PHP fatal that could break sign-in (login form, My account, and magic-link) on sites using the identity/attribution layer, corrects an AI credit balance that over-reported when a top-up was held, and removes a latent fatal on the paid-order path.
upgrade_notice.9.0: The plugin is now called Rooster One. Display name only — settings, data, shortcodes and block names are unchanged, and there is nothing to reconfigure. Also: one unified checkout newsletter opt-in instead of two, a tidier birthday field, accessibility fixes on ratings and promo links, and faster Largest Contentful Paint on category, page and blog heroes.
upgrade_notice.8.7: Makes more of Rooster One's native blocks (Recommendations, Product Slider, Product Variations Gallery) discoverable in the block editor and on the plugin page, documents the full block library, and clarifies the "Post Related Product Categories" block name. No front-end changes.
upgrade_notice.8.6: New: an in-chat SEO Auto-Fix Assistant with Google Search Console plus backlinks & disavow, a sharper and more relevant storefront assistant, and lower embedding costs. Much faster nightly Data Prep, vitals and analytics queries — no more billion-row scans or midnight swap spikes — and more resilient under heavy crawling. Note: the consent cookie scanner now defaults to off — rebuild the inventory on demand via "Re-scan storefront now".

aieo/sale-eligibility-message.description: Conditional badge that appears under the price WHEN the current product is on sale, telling the shopper how they qualify for the sale price (everyone, signed-in only, PRO role, etc.). Auto-hides on non-sale products. Token replacement: {regular_price}, {sale_price}, {savings_amount}, {savings_pct}, {role}.

messageProMember.default: 💎 Ως PRO μέλος δικαιούστε αυτή την τιμή σε κάθε παραγγελία.

aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.name: aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero
aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.title: AIEO Taxonomy Archive Hero
aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.description: Generic per-term archive hero. Auto-detects queried taxonomy (product_brand / pa_need / product_tag / product_cat) and dispatches to the right data source — brand vitals + extras for product_brand, need_extras for pa_need, term thumbnail + description for product_tag, category extras for product_cat. Filterable via aieo_taxonomy_archive_hero_data for new taxonomies.

aieo/popup-panel.name: aieo/popup-panel
aieo/popup-panel.title: AIEO Popup Panel
aieo/popup-panel.description: The split layout for a popup: a content pane you fill with any blocks, and a full-bleed image pane that sits beside it on desktop and moves above it on mobile — with a separate mobile image so a landscape photo never gets cropped to nothing on a phone. Built for the aieo_popup post type, but usable inline on any page.

aieo/post-related-needs.name: aieo/post-related-needs
aieo/post-related-needs.title: AIEO Post Related Needs
aieo/post-related-needs.description: Need-tag chips for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for pa_need → post edges. Each chip links to the need archive.

aieo/brand-slider.name: aieo/brand-slider
aieo/brand-slider.title: AIEO Brand Slider
aieo/brand-slider.description: Lazy-hydrated brand carousel. Modes: top, new_brand, new_product, favourites (per-user affinity), manual. Server-renders the first N cards as a noscript fallback; client hydrates into a vanilla scroll-snap carousel with arrow nav.

aieo/product-card-swatches.name: aieo/product-card-swatches
aieo/product-card-swatches.title: AIEO Product Swatches
aieo/product-card-swatches.description: Variation swatches for a product. Inside a block product loop it picks up the current product automatically; anywhere else, set a product ID. Renders the same cached swatch HTML every other placement uses.

aieo/product-variations-gallery.name: aieo/product-variations-gallery
aieo/product-variations-gallery.title: AIEO Product Variations Gallery
aieo/product-variations-gallery.description: Variation-aware product gallery: when a shopper selects a variation, the main product image and its gallery swap in place to that variation's own images. Reads each variation's existing image set, so there is no data migration.

aieo/lowest-price-message.name: aieo/lowest-price-message
aieo/lowest-price-message.title: AIEO Lowest Price Message
aieo/lowest-price-message.description: EU Omnibus: on on-sale products, shows the operator-configured message with the lowest price before the reduction. Auto-hides when the product is not on sale.

aieo/brand-related.name: aieo/brand-related
aieo/brand-related.title: AIEO Brand Related
aieo/brand-related.description: Cross-link strip for the brand archive: related product categories (chips), related blog articles (3-card row), and 'other brands you love' for logged-in viewers. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations + customer brand affinity.

aieo/brand-archive-hero.name: aieo/brand-archive-hero
aieo/brand-archive-hero.title: AIEO Brand Archive Hero
aieo/brand-archive-hero.description: Per-brand hero for the brand archive (taxonomy-product_brand). Reads queried brand term, joins core_brand_vitals + dmm_brand_extras. Renders hero image, logo overlay, headline, product count, wishlist heart, rating stars.

aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.name: aieo/taxonomy-related-articles
aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.title: AIEO Taxonomy Related Articles
aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.description: Renders 'From the Blog' article cards related to the queried term — works for any taxonomy (product_cat, pa_need, product_tag, supplier, custom). Reads bidirectional edges from wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations (the same source brand-related uses for product_brand). On the brand archive itself, prefer aieo/brand-related — this block is for the OTHER taxonomies.

aieo/recos.name: aieo/recos
aieo/recos.title: AIEO Recommendations
aieo/recos.description: Renders one AIEO recommendation surface (same_needs / crosssells / upsells / related / recently_viewed / semantic_related) as the placeholder div the lazy-recommendations.js bundle hydrator picks up on first user interaction. Same emitted markup as the legacy inline `<div id="aieo-X-placeholder">` blocks so the existing JS hydrator works unchanged.

aieo/loyalty-connection.name: aieo/loyalty-connection
aieo/loyalty-connection.title: AIEO Loyalty Connection
aieo/loyalty-connection.description: Bonus-card loyalty — connect/identify, then show the most recent points.

aieo/event-registration.name: aieo/event-registration
aieo/event-registration.title: Event Registration
aieo/event-registration.description: A self-registration form for an event — guests sign up by email and are taken to their RSVP page. Auto-binds to the event it's placed on, or pick a specific event.

aieo/brand-story.name: aieo/brand-story
aieo/brand-story.title: AIEO Brand Story
aieo/brand-story.description: Renders brand long-form copy (history, ambassadors, importer, footer) on the brand archive page. Reads queried brand term + wp_aieo_dmm_brand_extras. Emits nothing for sections with no copy.

aieo/semantic-related.name: aieo/semantic-related
aieo/semantic-related.title: AIEO Related content
aieo/semantic-related.description: Related articles, guides and products, chosen by the semantic engine.

aieo/breadcrumb.name: aieo/breadcrumb
aieo/breadcrumb.title: AIEO Breadcrumb
aieo/breadcrumb.description: SEO-consistent breadcrumb. Uses the SAME pinned canonical category as AIEO's canonical URL and JSON-LD BreadcrumbList, so the visible trail never disagrees with what Google reads.

aieo/free-shipping-pdp.name: aieo/free-shipping-pdp
aieo/free-shipping-pdp.title: AIEO Free Shipping (PDP bar)
aieo/free-shipping-pdp.description: Per-product free-shipping progress bar. Reads threshold + messages + appearance from AIEO_DMM_Free_Shipping (admin: DMM → Free Shipping + COD) and the current cart subtotal from WC()->cart. Self-hides when the operator's `display_product` setting is off, when the threshold is 0, when the product is on the no-free-shipping exclusion list, or when the cart is empty AND the operator chose to suppress the empty-cart message. Updates client-side on every cart change via a tiny REST poll.

aieo/latest-posts-overlay.name: aieo/latest-posts-overlay
aieo/latest-posts-overlay.title: AIEO Latest Posts Overlay
aieo/latest-posts-overlay.description: Latest blog posts with image overlay + category badge. Mobile: horizontal slider with bullet nav. Desktop: grid.

aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.name: aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer
aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.title: AIEO Taxonomy Archive Footer
aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.description: Per-term editorial / SEO footer copy. Reads the queried taxonomy's *_extras table footer column when present (need_extras.footer_text, brand_extras.footer_text, category_extras.footer_text). Emits nothing when no footer copy exists for the term.

aieo/professional-signup.name: aieo/professional-signup
aieo/professional-signup.title: AIEO Professional Signup
aieo/professional-signup.description: Professional / student registration via Gravity Forms (renders [membership_gf]).

aieo/custom-slots-region.name: aieo/custom-slots-region
aieo/custom-slots-region.title: AIEO Custom Slots Region
aieo/custom-slots-region.description: Placeholder block that, at render time, enumerates every enabled slot from the Custom Slots admin store and emits each as a sibling div. Designed to sit inside the .ff-recommendations-cluster flex container so each slot participates in the Recommendations Ordering CSS (`order:` / `display:none`) alongside the built-in aieo/recos rails. This block emits NO wrapper of its own — slot divs are direct flex children of the parent group.

aieo/product-slider.name: aieo/product-slider
aieo/product-slider.title: AIEO Product Slider
aieo/product-slider.description: A horizontal product slider with the SAME look as the product-page recommendations (thin uppercase title + line, then cards). Set the title manually and pick products by category, tag and/or specific product IDs.

aieo/brand-azindex.name: aieo/brand-azindex
aieo/brand-azindex.title: AIEO Brand A-Z Index
aieo/brand-azindex.description: Server-rendered A-Z brand directory. Every letter A–Z (plus '#' for non-Latin brands) is always present; empty letters render disabled. Sticky letter bar + per-letter brand grid with product counts. Reads exclusively from wp_aieo_core_brand_vitals.

aieo/post-related-brands.name: aieo/post-related-brands
aieo/post-related-brands.title: AIEO Post Related Brands
aieo/post-related-brands.description: Brand-logo slider for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for product_brand → post edges.

aieo/post-related-categories.name: aieo/post-related-categories
aieo/post-related-categories.title: AIEO Post Related Product Categories
aieo/post-related-categories.description: Dropdown of related product categories for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for product_cat → post edges.

aieo/competition.name: aieo/competition
aieo/competition.title: Competition
aieo/competition.description: Renders a competition — hero image, title, short description, the entry form and share buttons. Auto-binds to the competition page it's placed on, or pick a specific competition.

aieo/custom-slot.name: aieo/custom-slot
aieo/custom-slot.title: AIEO Custom Slot
aieo/custom-slot.description: Renders one operator-defined slot (Tolstoy widget OR free-form HTML/code) from the Custom Slots admin store. Used inside the single-product recommendations cluster so each slot can be drag-positioned alongside the built-in reco rails. Resolve target via slotId.

aieo/brand-rails.name: aieo/brand-rails
aieo/brand-rails.title: AIEO Brand Rails
aieo/brand-rails.description: Stacked curated brand rails (Featured / New / Your Favourites / Top). Each rail has its own count and slides-per-view, configurable in the inspector.

aieo/post-meta.name: aieo/post-meta
aieo/post-meta.title: AIEO Product Post Meta (SKU + Barcodes)
aieo/post-meta.description: Renders the SKU + per-variation barcode rows for the current product. Wraps AIEO_DMM_Product_Meta — the same module the `[om_ppe_product_meta]` shortcode uses (admin-configurable via DMM settings: show_sku, show_barcode, label customisation). On variable products the barcode row expands to one barcode per variation, hidden behind a `+ more` toggle.

aieo/product-needs.name: aieo/product-needs
aieo/product-needs.title: AIEO Product Needs
aieo/product-needs.description: Renders the 'This product covers:' Επιθυμίες (needs) list for the current single-product page. Wraps the existing AIEO_DMM_Product_Needs renderer so non-block themes keep their PHP path; on a block-themed PDP this is the canonical entry. Reads from `wp_aieo_dmm_product_needs` and `pa_need` taxonomy.

aieo/category-hero.name: aieo/category-hero
aieo/category-hero.title: AIEO Category Hero
aieo/category-hero.description: The queried category's hero — image, title and description — auto-filled from the term, for product or blog category archive headers.

aieo/category-chips.name: aieo/category-chips
aieo/category-chips.title: AIEO Category Chips
aieo/category-chips.description: A row of clickable category chips for the current archive — the term's child categories.

aieo/category-footer-hero.name: aieo/category-footer-hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.title: AIEO Category Footer Hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.description: The category's SEO footer text beside the category image (image left, rich text right) with the hero divider line. Auto-fills from the queried product category.

aieo/blog-hero.name: aieo/blog-hero
aieo/blog-hero.title: AIEO Blog Hero (Latest Post)
aieo/blog-hero.description: Featured latest-post hero with the category-hero look: a top title, the newest post's title as the headline, its excerpt as the description and its featured image — all clickable. On a blog category/tag archive it features that term's latest post.

aieo/page-hero.name: aieo/page-hero
aieo/page-hero.title: AIEO Page Hero
aieo/page-hero.description: Manual hero — top title, left headline, right description and desktop/mobile images. Identical look to the category hero, usable on any page.

aieo/category-lead.name: aieo/category-lead
aieo/category-lead.title: AIEO Category Lead
aieo/category-lead.description: The current category's description, falling back to its name when it has none. For blog category archive headers.

aieo/blog-subcategories.name: aieo/blog-subcategories
aieo/blog-subcategories.title: AIEO Blog Subcategories (Dropdown)
aieo/blog-subcategories.description: A dropdown of the current blog category's subcategories, styled like the blog-post categories dropdown. Renders nothing when the category has none.
